description: Gold evaluation set for the multi-domain corpus. Every answerable item was checked against the extracted document text. 'evidence' lists exact phrases (whitespace-insensitive, case-insensitive); a retrieved chunk counts as relevant if it comes from one of 'source_documents' and contains any evidence phrase. Unanswerable items must be refused.

items.question: What were Apple's total net sales in fiscal year 2025?

items.question: What was Apple's net income for fiscal 2025?
items.reference_answer: Apple's net income was $112,010 million in fiscal 2025.

items.question: How many full-time equivalent employees did Apple have at the end of fiscal 2025?
items.reference_answer: As of September 27, 2025, Apple had approximately 166,000 full-time equivalent employees.

items.question: What share of Apple's 2025 net sales went through indirect distribution channels?
items.reference_answer: 60% of total net sales came through indirect channels (40% through direct channels).

items.question: What was Microsoft's total revenue in fiscal year 2025?

items.question: How many people did Microsoft employ full-time as of June 30, 2025?
items.reference_answer: About 228,000 people full-time: 125,000 in the U.S. and 103,000 internationally.

items.question: By how much did Microsoft Cloud revenue grow in fiscal 2025?

items.question: What was the revenue of Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment in fiscal 2025?

items.question: Wie hoch war der Nettogewinn (net income) von Microsoft im Geschäftsjahr 2025?

items.question: Who is the Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft according to its 10-K?
items.reference_answer: Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (CEO since February 2014).

items.question: How does the NIST Generative AI Profile define confabulation?
items.reference_answer: The production of confidently stated but erroneous or false content (colloquially 'hallucinations' or 'fabrications') by which users may be misled or deceived.

items.question: What does CBRN stand for in NIST AI 600-1?
items.reference_answer: Chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (weapons or other dangerous materials or agents).

items.question: Which impacts does the NIST GenAI profile describe under the Data Privacy risk?
items.reference_answer: Leakage and unauthorized use, disclosure, or de-anonymization of biometric, health, location, or other personally identifiable information or sensitive data.

items.question: What environmental impacts of generative AI does NIST AI 600-1 describe?
items.reference_answer: Impacts due to high compute resource utilization in training or operating GAI models, and related outcomes that may adversely impact ecosystems.

items.question: Which earlier RFC does RFC 9111 obsolete?
items.reference_answer: RFC 9111 obsoletes RFC 7234.

items.question: For heuristic freshness based on Last-Modified, what fraction of the interval does RFC 9111 call a typical setting?
items.reference_answer: A typical setting of the fraction might be 10% of the interval since the last modification.

items.question: What does the no-store request directive tell an HTTP cache?
items.reference_answer: The cache MUST NOT store any part of either this request or any response to it.
evidence: store any part of either this request

items.question: What does a Kubernetes cluster consist of?
items.reference_answer: A control plane plus a set of worker machines (nodes) that run containerized applications; every cluster needs at least one worker node to run Pods.
evidence: control plane plus a set of worker machines

items.question: When does a Kubernetes node not need to run kube-proxy?
items.reference_answer: When a network plugin provides its own (third-party) implementation of proxying.

items.question: What does the Kubernetes Job controller do?
items.reference_answer: It watches for Job objects that represent one-off tasks and creates Pods to run those tasks to completion.

items.question: In GitHub Actions, what is a job?
items.reference_answer: A set of steps in a workflow that is executed on the same runner; each step is a shell script or an action.

items.question: Which operating systems does GitHub provide virtual machines for to run workflows?
items.reference_answer: Linux, Windows, and macOS (or you can host your own self-hosted runners).
evidence: Linux, Windows, and macOS virtual machines

items.question: What are the five focus areas of the AWS Well-Architected performance efficiency pillar?
items.reference_answer: Architecture selection; compute and hardware; data management; networking and content delivery; process and culture.

items.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
items.reference_answer: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.

items.question: Where does Delta Lake store checkpoint files?
items.reference_answer: Checkpoints are stored in the _delta_log directory and can be created for any committed version of the table.

items.question: What is the purpose of the Delta Lake last checkpoint file?
items.reference_answer: It reduces the cost of constructing the latest snapshot by pointing to near the end of the log, avoiding listing a huge _delta_log directory.
evidence: pointer to near the end of the log

items.question: Should writers still create multi-part checkpoints in Delta Lake?
items.reference_answer: No. Multi-part checkpoints are deprecated; writers should use uuid-named V2 spec checkpoints instead.

items.question: Which new capabilities does Iceberg format version 3 add?
items.reference_answer: New data types (nanosecond timestamps, unknown, variant, geometry, geography), column default values, multi-argument transforms, row lineage tracking, binary deletion vectors and table encryption keys.

items.question: In Apache Iceberg, where are the manifests that make up a snapshot stored?
items.reference_answer: In a manifest list file, which stores metadata about the manifests such as partition stats and data file counts.
evidence: stored in a manifest list file

items.question: Which SQL clauses does Spark support for Iceberg time travel queries?
items.reference_answer: TIMESTAMP AS OF and VERSION AS OF.

items.question: What can the VERSION AS OF clause contain in Iceberg Spark queries?
items.reference_answer: A long snapshot ID or a string branch or tag name.
evidence: snapshot ID or a string branch or tag name

items.question: What is a row group in Parquet?
items.reference_answer: A logical horizontal partitioning of the data into rows; it consists of a column chunk for each column.

items.question: What row group size does the Parquet format documentation recommend?
items.reference_answer: Large row groups of 512MB to 1GB; an optimized read setup is 1GB row groups with a 1GB HDFS block size.

items.question: What buffer alignment and padding does the Arrow columnar format recommend?
items.reference_answer: Allocate memory on aligned addresses with lengths that are a multiple of 8 or 64 bytes; 64-byte padding is recommended (e.g. for SIMD).

items.question: How is the null count of an Arrow array represented?
items.reference_answer: As a 64-bit signed integer.

items.question: What is the recommended way to declare task dependencies in an Airflow DAG?
items.reference_answer: Use the >> and << (bitshift) operators, e.g. first_task >> [second_task, third_task].

items.question: Which system is PostgreSQL based on?
items.reference_answer: POSTGRES Version 4.2, developed at the University of California at Berkeley Computer Science Department; PostgreSQL is an object-relational DBMS.

items.question: What is a Dataset in Spark SQL?
items.reference_answer: A distributed collection of data.
evidence: A Dataset is a distributed collection of data

items.question: What must an OpenAPI 3.1 document contain at a minimum?
items.reference_answer: At least one of: a paths field, a components field, or a webhooks field.

items.question: What uniqueness rule applies to operationId in OpenAPI?
items.reference_answer: It MUST be unique among all operations described in the API, and it is case-sensitive.
evidence: MUST be unique among all operations

items.question: What are the two primary data structures in pandas?
items.reference_answer: Series, a one-dimensional labeled array, and DataFrame, a two-dimensional data structure like a table.

items.question: Which Python operator performs floor division?
items.reference_answer: The // operator (e.g. 17 // 3 gives 5); / always returns a float.

items.question: Can you change a single character inside a Python string?

items.question: According to PEP 484, how should a type checker treat a function without annotations?
items.reference_answer: As having the most general type possible, or it should be ignored by the type checker.
